audience: Bank or institutional buyer credit, treasury, legal, operations, settlement and technology teams
corePromise: Receive a better-structured portfolio and traceable evidence record while retaining every buyer decision and control.

slides.title: A controlled preparation layer for conventional direct assignment
slides.purpose: Position AssureRail as evidence, workflow and coordination infrastructure between seller preparation and the buyer's own diligence.
claims: AssureRail does not make the bank's credit, legal, compliance, valuation, pricing or purchase decision.

slides.title: Why smaller portfolios create disproportionate buyer effort
slides.purpose: Show format variation, incomplete histories, evidence gaps, repeated questions and settlement dependencies.
slides.visual: Buyer effort by preparation quality, without an unverified market-size claim

slides.title: Buyer access starts after an executed MSA
slides.purpose: Show institutional approval, administrator nomination, MFA, scoped roles, profile approval and synthetic workspace test.
claims: No public buyer self-registration creates authority or portfolio access.

slides.title: Your requirements are structured, versioned and approved
slides.purpose: Show multi-select asset/originator options, ranges for corpus/concentration/performance, controlled diligence choices and hover definitions.
slides.visual: Compact buyer settings sections with checkboxes for non-exclusive choices
claims: Free text is limited to bounded exceptions.

slides.title: Buyer policy becomes traceable preparation checks
slides.purpose: Explain the allow-listed decision-table compiler and record-level results.
slides.visual: MSA/profile citation → predicate → loan/borrower/document result → exception
claims: Unknown evidence never silently passes and no arbitrary buyer expression executes.

slides.title: Full-population computation and professional work stay distinct
slides.purpose: Show recorded outcomes for each admitted loan beside disclosed legal, CA, field or technical samples.
claims: Computational coverage is not a claim that every source fact or asset was independently verified.

slides.title: A buyer-ready evidence pack arrives with its exceptions
slides.purpose: Show tape/source reconciliation, repayment and arrears history, documents, KYC/authority, security, insurance, debt-release and originator information.
slides.visual: Evidence families, version/digest, status, gaps and reviewer ownership

slides.title: AI organises evidence; rules and accountable people decide
slides.purpose: Show source-grounded findings, run receipts, abstentions, deterministic checks and expert boundaries.
claims: Initial Assessment is automated and unsigned.
Qualified professionals sign only their Portfolio Preparation sections.

slides.title: Diligence questions remain attributable and closeable
slides.purpose: Show source-linked question, owner, requested evidence, priority, response, reviewer involvement and closure.
claims: Standard acknowledgement target: one business day; substantive response target: five business days when no new external act is required, subject to MSA.

slides.title: Secure file exchange first; APIs only where justified
slides.purpose: Present low-friction per-buyer SFTP with host pinning, manifest digests, maker-checker, idempotency and acknowledgements.
slides.visual: Sandbox profile → approved export → buyer acknowledgement → reconciliation
claims: ₹50,000 is the seller-paid standard accepted point-to-point connection fee; APIs are quoted on request.
No production connection before the buyer's sandbox and security acceptance.

slides.title: Closing instructions are balanced and separately authorised
slides.purpose: Show CP evidence, final document slots, exact seller-specific waterfall and separate seller/buyer approval.
slides.visual: Buyer funding → appointed bank/VAN → debt release, AssureRail fee, approved external legs and seller net
claims: AssureRail records provider observations and ambiguity repair; it does not hold funds or unilaterally release them.

slides.title: RBAC follows institution, workspace, case, document and action
slides.purpose: Show Primary Administrator, Deal Lead, Credit, Legal, Settlement, Monitoring and Auditor roles with maker-checker controls.
claims: A user in one buyer workspace receives no access to another buyer or an uninvited case.

slides.title: Monitoring is a selected service, not an automatic seller charge
slides.purpose: Show one-time closing baseline and optional ongoing monitoring, payer and servicer dependencies.
claims: For DA, year two onward is normally buyer-funded unless the seller remains servicer or documents state another allocation.

slides.title: Agree one structured pilot framework
slides.purpose: Request an MSA design session covering eligibility, evidence, users, SFTP, Q&A, settlement, monitoring and acceptance tests.
slides.visual: Decision checklist with named bank owners across credit, legal, operations, settlement, technology and procurement
claims: A profile or pilot acceptance is not a commitment to purchase any pool.

mustInclude: Record-level buyer-policy compiler and UNKNOWN handling
Evidence provenance and AI run receipts
Seller-specific coordinated closing and no-custody boundary
mustExclude: Bank logos, HDFC or Axis names without written permission
Any implication that a buyer endorsed the product or committed to purchase
Internal 60 bps benchmark or seller referral economics
PTC, tokenisation, multi-signature or Plaza as current DA dependencies
Atomic settlement, risk-free, guaranteed compliance or guaranteed data-quality claims
Raw prompt, model or infrastructure detail that does not help the bank make a decision
